title: An Algebraic Approach to Quantum Field Theory
section_locator: Abstract; pp. 848-861; scanned primary PDF text checked at https://electronicsandbooks.com/edt/manual/Magazine/J/Journal%20of%20Mathematical%20Physics/PDF/V05/JMP1964V05N07.pdf
assumptions: Axiomatic algebraic formulation assigning algebras of observables to spacetime regions; the article discusses isotony, locality and covariance in a fixed Minkowski setting. The exact conventional net axiom list was not fully transcribed from the scanned copy in this pass.
conclusion: Advocates local observable algebras as the central structure and argues that faithful representations of the same abstract observable algebra can express physical equivalence despite unitary inequivalence. The framework encodes which observables are local and their inclusion/commutation relations; it does not specify a temporal ontology or passage.
proof_status: Conceptual framework paper; no theorem proof independently reconstructed.
dependencies: Mathematical setting: abstract observable *-algebras and their faithful Hilbert-space representations; assignment of observable algebras to spacetime regions and the stated locality/covariance structure. These are the framework's own ingredients, not an externally audited theorem dependency.
open_questions: A later exact axiom-by-axiom extraction from Haag (1996) or a primary formalization would be useful; no such claim is needed for this lane.
relevance: Baseline locality/net model and limits of what local algebra structure alone says about time.
limits: Full scanned article text was available, but some OCR/math is noisy. Do not read the source as proving that locality entails eternalism, presentism, or objective becoming. No relevant related source record in this lane is an input to the paper; related_source_ids is therefore intentionally empty.

title: Bemerkungen zur unitäräquivalenz von lorentzinvarianten Feldern
version: Il Nuovo Cimento 22(5), 1051-1068 (1961); DOI 10.1007/BF02787889 verified against MaRDI/zbMATH metadata, text unread
relevance: Original Reeh–Schlieder source for vacuum cyclicity and the nontrivial limits on interpreting local operations as producing spatially localized states.
limits: Original full text not obtained; bibliographic lead only. The theorem assumptions below are taken from the full-text later exposition aqft-fewster-rejzner-2020v2, not attributed to an unaudited exact statement in this original.

title: Algebraic Quantum Field Theory – an introduction
version: arXiv:1904.04051v2, 18 November 2019; published in Progress and Visions in Quantum Theory in View of Gravity (Birkhäuser, 2020)
section_locator: Sec. 4.1 basic AQFT requirements; Sec. 5.2, Theorem 26 and proof, pp. 25-27 of v2 PDF; Sec. 6.3 local experiments can be prepared locally
assumptions: For the Reeh–Schlieder theorem as stated in Sec. 5.2: a Poincaré-covariant Haag–Kastler net in a vacuum representation, positive-energy/spectrum condition, translation-invariant vacuum cyclic for the global algebra, weak additivity, and a nonempty region with a smaller open region whose sufficiently small translates remain inside. Einstein causality plus an open region in the causal complement gives separation. Full precise statement is source-located; hypotheses summarized here rather than independently formalized.
conclusion: The vacuum is cyclic for each such local algebra; if the causal complement has interior and Einstein causality holds, it is also separating. Cyclicity means norm-approximation of arbitrary Hilbert vectors by AΩ with A in the local algebra, not that an implementable, energy-bounded, deterministic, or no-signaling operation locally prepares an arbitrary distant state. Sec. 6.3 distinguishes state-vector approximation from local experiment preparation and uses extra operational structure.
proof_status: Authors provide a proof in the cited section; statement and proof section inspected, not independently reproduced.
dependencies: Reeh–Schlieder derivation uses Poincaré covariance, positive-energy translation spectrum, invariant vacuum, global cyclicity, weak additivity and local commutativity as stated in Sec. 5.2; separation additionally uses a nonempty causal complement. These are theorem premises, not a new result.
open_questions: Theorem versions vary in region regularity and additivity assumptions; any use beyond the stated vacuum-net hypotheses needs an exact matching result. Quantitative cost/energy bounds are not supplied by cyclicity alone.
relevance: Provides explicit Reeh–Schlieder assumptions and distinguishes cyclicity from operationally implementable local experiments.
limits: Pedagogical exposition of established theory rather than an original proof paper. The authors explicitly say algebraic states need not all be physically realizable (Sec. 2.3); no inference from dense orbit to superluminal signaling is licensed.

title: Tomita's Theory of Modular Hilbert Algebras and its Applications
version: Lecture Notes in Mathematics 128, Springer (1970); DOI 10.1007/BFb0065832
relevance: Foundational exposition of Tomita–Takesaki modular theory: for a von Neumann algebra with a cyclic and separating vector, the modular objects generate an intrinsic one-parameter automorphism group and identify the commutant via modular conjugation.
limits: Bibliographic and metadata discovery only in this lane; theorem statement and proof not directly audited from Takesaki. The algebraic theorem is stated in the inspected original Bisognano–Wichmann 1975 paper, pp. 998-999, and should be used as the exact locator here.

title: On the Duality Condition for a Hermitian Scalar Field
version: Journal of Mathematical Physics 16(4), 985-1007 (1975); DOI 10.1063/1.522605; scanned primary copy https://denebola.if.usp.br/~jbarata/leituras-recomendadas/BisognanoWichmann-01-DualityConditionHermitianScalarField_985_1_online.pdf
section_locator: Secs. II-IV, Theorems 1-2, especially pp. 990-998; modular-theory statement pp. 998-999; wedge-duality assumptions pp. 1000-1002
assumptions: The paper works in four-dimensional Minkowski space with a separable physical Hilbert space, strongly continuous unitary proper-Poincaré representation, translation spectrum in the closed forward cone, unique translation-invariant vacuum, and a local Hermitian scalar operator-valued tempered-distribution field. The modular-algebra conclusion additionally requires a wedge von Neumann algebra with vacuum cyclic and invariant under the wedge-preserving boosts; the authors explicitly say existence/adequate size of such algebras is not automatic under their minimal field assumptions (pp. 986, 1002). Exact 1975 result is formulated through analytic continuation of boosts and TCP, then the modular operator relation, not as a blanket claim for any AQFT net.
conclusion: For the right wedge, the modular flow in the vacuum representation is the Lorentz boost subgroup preserving the wedge, with convention-dependent 2π normalization; modular conjugation is tied to TCP/reflection. Wedge duality follows only under additional algebra-existence/density premises discussed in the paper. The modular parameter is a state-and-algebra-dependent automorphism parameter identified geometrically in this special setting; it is not generic observer clock time, a universal time coordinate, or objective passage.
proof_status: Original paper full text inspected, including assumptions, theorem statements, and caveats; proof not independently reconstructed. The generalized modern BW theorem for arbitrary nets is not audited here.
dependencies: Tomita's modular theorem for a von Neumann algebra with cyclic-separating vector supplies J and the modular unitary group (BW pp. 998-999); the physical identification additionally uses the paper's Poincaré representation, forward spectrum, vacuum, scalar-field locality/analyticity and wedge-algebra premises recorded in assumptions.
open_questions: Compare exact theorem variants for general Wightman fields, graded-local nets, curved spacetimes, and representations without BW property before transferring the conclusion.
relevance: Sharp test case for the difference between modular flow and physical clock time.
limits: The title concerns duality, and the field/algebra domain assumptions matter. No universal modular Hamiltonian/local geometric flow is implied for bounded regions or arbitrary states.

title: Algebraic quantum field theory in curved spacetimes
version: arXiv:1504.00586v1 (2015); chapter in Advances in Algebraic Quantum Field Theory, Birkhäuser (2015), DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-21353-8_4
section_locator: Secs. 2-3 (locally covariant functor, local covariance, Einstein causality and time-slice); Sec. 5 and Sec. 7.6 (partial Reeh–Schlieder transfer); Sec. 11.3 (natural states no-go)
assumptions: Models a theory as a covariant functor from globally hyperbolic, oriented and time-oriented spacetimes with causally convex isometric embeddings to unital *-algebras; supplements functoriality with Einstein causality and the time-slice axiom. Specific results require further named hypotheses; see individual theorem records/locators.
conclusion: Local covariance structures local observables across spacetimes and compatible embeddings; it does not select a preferred foliation or unique state. Cauchy morphisms encode dynamical equivalence between globally hyperbolic regions sharing Cauchy data. This is a precise covariance/locality framework, not a metaphysical theory of becoming.
proof_status: Full chapter text inspected selectively at the stated sections; individual theorem proof audits are separately marked below.
dependencies: Mathematical framework: the Loc/Alg functorial setup, causally convex isometric embeddings, Einstein causality and the time-slice property; the chapter explicitly builds on the BFV locally covariant framework. Individual results have additional hypotheses given at their own locators.
open_questions: What extra structure would empirically distinguish observer-limited records from a complete algebraic history is not addressed by the framework itself.
relevance: Curved-spacetime comparison model for local covariance, dynamics, and records.
limits: This source is a review chapter, not an original result paper. Functorial locality/time-slice assumptions encode causal propagation but do not by themselves imply a temporal ontology. Stable lane ID retains the original `2012` label but is misleading: this record is the 2015 arXiv 1504.00586v1 chapter.

title: Dynamical locality and covariance: What makes a physical theory the same in all spacetimes?
section_locator: Secs. 2-3 definitions; Sec. 6, Definition 6.1 dynamical locality, Theorems 6.10 and 6.13; Theorem 6.13 proof, lines 1022-1045 in arXiv HTML v3
assumptions: Theorem 6.13: a dynamically local theory in the authors' Loc functor category has a natural state assignment compatible with every spacetime morphism; on some spacetime with noncompact Cauchy surfaces, that state's GNS representation is faithful and has the Reeh–Schlieder cyclicity property for every relatively compact region. Under these premises relative Cauchy evolution is trivial there. If extended locality also holds, the theory is equivalent to the trivial theory. Paper's definitions of Loc, timeslice, dynamical locality, and extended locality apply.
conclusion: Kinematic local subalgebras and dynamical local subalgebras (observables insensitive to metric perturbations in the causal complement) coincide in dynamically local theories. The conditional no-natural-state theorem constrains a covariant preferred state in all spacetimes, not local records or passage directly. The conclusion follows from covariance, local response and cyclicity premises; it is not a no-go for every state selection on a single spacetime.
proof_status: Theorem statement and proof inspected in primary text; proof not independently reconstructed. Exact condition that cyclicity, faithfulness, noncompact Cauchy surface, and extended locality each enter is recorded.
dependencies: Builds on the BFV locally covariant theory category and time-slice framework; uses kinematic local subobjects, relative Cauchy evolution under metric perturbations, dynamical locality, GNS representations, Reeh–Schlieder cyclicity and (for the final equivalence conclusion) extended locality. Theorem 6.13 premises are enumerated in this record.
open_questions: Test the theorem against specific state spaces and theories only after verifying dynamical locality and faithfulness; theorem does not decide whether objective becoming exists.
relevance: Main audited result linking covariance, localized dynamical response and state selection.
limits: Authors explicitly present SPASs principles as necessary, not exhaustive. No inference to ontology, determinism, a thermodynamic arrow, or observer-access limits follows.

title: Dynamical locality of the free scalar field
section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 4, Theorem 4.3 and adjacent construction/proof, lines 406-422 in arXiv HTML
assumptions: The paper defines the massless minimally coupled scalar theory modulo locally constant solutions, in the locally covariant framework, and distinguishes categories Loc (possibly disconnected spacetimes) and Loc_0 (connected spacetimes). The theorem is specific to that quotient model and those categories.
conclusion: The quotient massless scalar theory is dynamically local in Loc_0 for all spacetime dimensions n>=2 and in Loc for n>=3, but not in Loc at n=2. The authors exhibit the two-dimensional disconnected-spacetime topological obstruction; they conjecture adding topological charge as background may address it. This is a model/domain-specific locality result, not a universal claim about local events.
proof_status: Theorem 4.3 statement and explanatory derivation inspected; no independent reproduction.
dependencies: Uses the locally covariant functor/time-slice and relative-Cauchy-evolution framework, the classical minimally coupled Klein–Gordon solution space, its symplectic structure, and the quotient by locally constant solutions. The comparison target is kinematic versus dynamical localization as defined in the Fewster–Verch framework.
open_questions: The paper identifies topological charge as a conjectural diagnosis of the two-dimensional failure; keep the authors' conjecture separate from theorem content.
relevance: Concrete counterexample to treating kinematic and dynamical localization as automatically identical.
limits: Massless scalar quotient model only; do not generalize the dimensional exception to all AQFTs.
